A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, despite the changed title and renaming of FACT to CLAM. The shared formulation, experiments, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original ResNet-50 experiments on five classification datasets, including fairness metrics, worst-class accuracies, overall accuracies, and training curves.

after.justification: V3 retains original five-dataset experiments and reports additional augmentation-effect, class-weight evolution, and APStar comparison results.

M1.justification: After matching v2's projected weight notation with v3's weight variable, the practical procedure remains weighted-loss training with epochwise, clipped multiplicative updates based on training accuracies. V2 Equation (10) and Algorithm 1 correspond to v3 Equation (8) and Algorithm 2; renaming and separating theoretical from practical descriptions do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Fashion-MNIST, Mini-ImageNet, and ImageNet under the retained crop-strength coverage. The new analyses reuse these classification scenarios. Other architectures and multi-task applications are discussed, not evaluated.

E2.justification: The five main comparators remain, but TCE's class-weight update changes from normalized exponentiated losses to a smoothed update with gamma = 0.5 (v2 Appendix B; v3 Appendix C). V3 additionally evaluates APStar against CLAM in a CIFAR-100 stability comparison, shown in Appendix J.

E3.justification: V3 adds the accuracy-range difference with versus without augmentation, averaged over seven augmented crop settings (Table 2). The existing ResNet-50 setup, eight crop bounds from 0.48 to 1, dataset partitions, and stated training budgets remain unchanged. Revised range values alone do not establish a changed range definition.

E4.justification: V3 substantially expands the diagnostic analyses: Table 2 examines augmentation-induced disparity changes; Figure 4 and Appendix I track class weights alongside accuracies; Appendix J compares CLAM and APStar stability. These investigate augmentation effects and optimization behavior beyond v2's worst-class and fairness-over-training analyses.

E5.justification: Both report means and standard deviations across crop settings and display variability in training curves. V3's additional table continues this practice. Neither version discloses random-seed replication, confidence intervals, or significance testing; changed standard-deviation values are result changes.

E6.justification: Several main results are revised: FACT/CLAM's CIFAR-100 range changes from 44.7 to 35.9, while TCE's average accuracy changes from 63.6 ± 23.8 to 74.7 ± 2.4 alongside its revised update rule. V3 also adds augmentation-difference and weight-dynamics/APStar findings. The proposed method's average and worst-10%-class accuracies remain unchanged across corresponding tables.

T1.justification: V3 adds Proposition 4.1 and Appendix A's proof of monotonicity, Schur-concavity, and symmetry under a permutation-closed weight domain. It also restricts Theorem 1's comparator to the constrained simplex and revises the KL-divergence derivation. The theorem drops v2's approximate qualifier, although Appendix B still uses approximation steps.

C1.justification: The central constrained-game formulation, improved worst-class performance, and limited overall-accuracy cost remain the main claims. V3 adds an explicit contribution claim that CLAM reduces the increase in class disparities with stronger augmentation, while focusing the framing more specifically on augmentation's class-dependent effects.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive explanations of unconstrained max-min oscillation, APStar's emphasis on difficult classes, architecture independence, and class-weight convergence. Section 4.4 also discusses poorer outcomes from validation-based updates and conjectures reduced training data and higher estimation variance as causes. The original fairness–accuracy limitation is retained.

D1.justification: V3 newly documents normalization of practical loss weights to sum to the number of classes, explains training-based weight updates, and specifies TCE's smoothing parameter and initialization. The proposed method's tau and clipping-threshold values, dataset access instructions, hardware, and training-time disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to distinguish fair optimization, sensitive-group fairness, and class equity. New discussion of Agarwal et al., Martinez et al./APStar, and Xu et al. positions the contribution against existing game-based fairness approaches. This materially revises the novelty context beyond bibliographic and citation-style updates.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites the introduction, related work, methodological explanations, and results narrative. It changes the title and FACT terminology, reorganizes related work, adds a practical-implementation subsection, and separates formal and practical algorithms. These are substantial editorial and structural changes.

P2.justification: V3 changes the document layout and substantially reorganizes exhibits. Figure 3 changes from four datasets to two, retained appendix plots are resized and redistributed, and new augmentation, weight-evolution, and APStar displays are added. The algorithm presentation expands into two separate displays.

improvement.justification: V3 improves the justification and interpretability of the work through explicit fairness properties, relevant prior-game comparisons, and targeted augmentation and weight-dynamics analyses. These gains are limited by new overstatement: Table 2's claim of uniformly lowest differences conflicts with TCE's better Mini-ImageNet value (−5.2 versus −3.5), and Theorem 1 is stated more firmly despite remaining approximation steps in Appendix B.
